name: Ascent

profile.address: North Point Parkway, Alpharetta, Fulton County, Georgia, 30009
profile.reading:
This building at 4905 North Point Parkway, at Kimball Bridge Road, in Alpharetta, Georgia was built in 2009 by BlackBerry (then Research In Motion) as a company data center, and its ownership history since then explains why this registry lists "Ascent" as operator even though the building no longer appears among Ascent's currently marketed properties. In February 2017, BlackBerry sold the roughly 40-acre property for $30 million to Ascent, a St. Louis-based data center operator, in partnership with TowerBrook Capital Partners; the deal included a partial leaseback letting BlackBerry keep operating space on site while Ascent took over the building, which it rebranded Ascent ATL1 and marketed for cloud and edge colocation tenants.

Ascent's ownership did not last: in 2022 the property was sold again, this time to a partnership between Lincoln Rackhouse -- the data center division of Lincoln Property Company -- and Principal Real Estate Investors. At that sale the building was described as 185,000 square feet on about 38 acres, with roughly 7 megawatts of live capacity expandable to 13 megawatts, and enough additional land on the site to support a new ground-up building of up to 30 megawatts. Under the new ownership structure, Ascent stayed on in an operating role -- continuing to provide facilities management, engineering, and construction services for the building -- while CBRE's Atlanta team and Digital Crossroad took over marketing and leasing to tenants. That arrangement is almost certainly why the underlying map data behind this registry still names Ascent as operator: Ascent runs the building day to day even though Lincoln Rackhouse and Principal, not Ascent, now own it, and Ascent's own current data center listings, which show only Toronto and Chicago facilities, no longer include Atlanta because it is not part of Ascent's owned portfolio.

No party in this chain of BlackBerry-to-Ascent-to-Lincoln Rackhouse/Principal ownership has published current tenant names, utilization, or a detailed cooling design for the building beyond the capacity figures disclosed at the 2022 sale, which is typical for a multi-tenant colocation asset that has changed hands through private commercial real estate transactions rather than public offerings. What is documented is the building's origin as BlackBerry's own facility, its 2017 conversion into third-party colocation space under Ascent, and its 2022 sale into a real-estate investment structure where Ascent remains the on-site operator rather than the owner -- a common pattern in colocation real estate that a facility's "operator" and its "owner" are not the same company, and that either can change without the other.

reading: Ascent is a data center facility and property management services company, founded in 1998, that designs, builds, operates, maintains, and repairs data center infrastructure on behalf of other companies rather than leasing colocation space directly to tenants. WESCO International, the publicly traded industrial distribution and services company listed on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker WCC, agreed in 2024 to acquire Ascent for 185 million dollars on a cash-free, debt-free basis, with the deal closing in December 2024. At the time of acquisition, Ascent reported 115 million dollars in trailing twelve month revenue with a 30 percent three-year compound annual growth rate, and employed more than 330 people across the United States and Canada. Ascent's flagship managed facility is a 310,000 square foot data center on 26 acres in Toronto with up to 60 megawatts of capacity, and the company built a proprietary software platform called Navigator for integrated infrastructure management dashboards used across its managed sites. Trade press coverage of the acquisition noted that Ascent had previously operated facilities in Chicago, Atlanta, and Plano, Texas that it no longer owned by the time of the WESCO deal, consistent with a facilities management business model where Ascent's relationship to a given building can change from owner to operator to former operator over time. This registry's Georgia facility record for Ascent, an Alpharetta site referenced in third-party directories as a former RIM building, should be understood in that context, as a managed or formerly managed site rather than a permanently owned asset, and reconciled carefully during the facility research phase rather than assumed to still be an active Ascent-operated site.
